mutations.because: `--switched-at` is a REQUIRED flag (req 4): a default would classify every campaign against an instant nobody chose. Deleting this guard does not let the run proceed — it falls into the UN-PARSEABLE refusal, because `new Date(undefined)` is an Invalid Date and the next line is exactly the check that says so. That is why the two refusals carry two different messages, and it is the only reason requirement 4's missing-flag test can tell which branch ran: it asserts `--switched-at <iso> is required` verbatim, and the mutant answers `--switched-at <iso> is not a valid date: "undefined"` instead. A single shared message would have made this mutation survive with the run still refusing, which is the difference between a missing flag being a fixable mistake and a missing flag being a mystery.
command: req 4: a MISSING --switched-at refuses with its own message

mutations.because: What this mutation proves is the DIAGNOSIS, and it is worth being exact about that, because the obvious reading of the branch is wrong. Deleting it does NOT restore the read-through hazard: `lstatSync` never follows a link, so `st.isFile()` is false for EVERY symlink and the following `!st.isFile()` branch already refuses one before any read. The safety half of this fix belongs to the choice of `lstat` over `stat`/`existsSync`, not to this branch. What the branch buys is that the two failures stay distinguishable. A link is answered `unsafe` + "the ref is a symlink; the importer never follows one", which tells the operator to remove the link; the mutant answers `refused-file` + "is not a regular file", which tells them to put a regular file there — and a file they create BESIDE the link leaves the link in place, still pointing wherever it pointed, still one `readFileSync` away from being read. The assertion that fails is the whole object: `kind` `unsafe` → `refused-file` and the reason string, on the symlink test only. The directory test is unaffected, and so is the dangling-symlink test in its KIND but not its reason — which is the point of pinning this branch rather than the `lstat` call: the link's own answer is what is under test.
command: a SYMLINK at the ref path is unsafe: the importer never follows one
